robins_wager.name: Robin's First Wager
robins_wager.intro: An old tale the band likes to tell: how young Robin of Locksley first crossed the King's foresters, and why he lives in the greenwood now.

nodes.text: Young Robin walks to Nottingham fair with his bow. Under a tree sit fifteen foresters, eating pies and boasting.
'Ho, boy! That toy bow couldn't hit a barn door!' The foresters laugh at him.

options.label: Wager he can hit the far oak
options.log: Robin bets them twenty shillings, draws, and splits a knot on an oak a hundred paces off.

options.label: Shrug and walk on
options.log: Robin walks on, but the foresters follow, jeering. He turns, shoots, and knocks the cap off the loudest one.

nodes.text: 'Seize the cheeky pup!' Two of the foresters come at him.
The foresters run for Nottingham, dropping their purse. Robin buys supper for the whole village, and from that day he is an outlaw of Sherwood.

will_meets_robin.name: The Stranger in Scarlet
will_meets_robin.intro: Around the fire, Will Scarlet tells how he and Robin first met, and both of them insist they won.

nodes.text: Robin, newly outlawed, sees a young man in fine scarlet strolling through the glade, sniffing a rose.
'Stand!' says Robin. The stranger yawns. 'Must I?'

options.label: Ask for a toll
options.log: 'A toll? From me?' The stranger draws his sword with a flourish.

options.label: Challenge him to a bout
options.log: 'A bout? Delightful.' The stranger draws his sword with a flourish.

nodes.text: Bow against blade in the glade!
nodes.win: Robin trips the stranger into a gorse bush. 'Ow! All right, all right!'
nodes.lose: The stranger flicks Robin's hood over his eyes. 'Shall we call it a draw?'

nodes.text: 'Will Gamwell is my name, Robin. I'm your own cousin, come to find you!' Ever after, the band calls him Will Scarlet.

gamwell_christmas.name: Christmas at Gamwell Hall
gamwell_christmas.intro: Will takes Robin home to his father's hall for Christmas. There's a yule log, plum pudding and games on the green.

nodes.text: Old Squire Gamwell hugs his son and pours Robin a mug of hot spiced cider.
The village gathers on the green for the Christmas games.

options.label: Join the cudgel play
options.log: Robin and Will knock over every challenger, and the village cheers.

options.label: Sing carols in the hall
options.log: Will sings loud and badly. Everyone joins in to drown him out.

nodes.text: A bailiff barges in. 'A Christmas tax, by order of the Sheriff! Hand over the pudding money!'
The bailiff runs off into the snow without his hat. The squire gives the band a cartload of Christmas cheer for Sherwood.

tanner.name: Arthur a Bland the Tanner
tanner.intro: A big tanner from Nottingham has been striding through Sherwood as if he owns it. Robin decides to have some fun.

nodes.text: Robin pulls his hood up and pretends to be a keeper of the King's forest.
'Who are you, bold fellow, to walk in the King's wood?' The tanner leans on his staff. 'Who are you to ask?'

options.label: Demand his name
options.log: 'My name? Make me tell you,' grins the tanner.

options.label: Measure staves
options.log: They measure their staves. The tanner's is longer. Robin cuts a longer one. The tanner laughs.

nodes.text: The tanner swings, and the oak leaves shake.
nodes.win: Robin's staff whacks the tanner's knuckles. 'Ow! Fair hit!'
nodes.lose: THWACK! Robin sits down in the ferns, seeing stars. 'Hold your hand! I'll own you're the better man.'

nodes.text: 'Arthur a Bland is my name.' He promises to tan leather jerkins for the whole band, free of charge.

golden_prize.name: Robin Hood's Golden Prize
golden_prize.intro: Two rich priests ride north, refusing every beggar on the road. Robin borrows a friar's robe.

nodes.text: Robin, dressed as a poor friar, hobbles up to the priests. 'A penny for a hungry brother?'
'We haven't a penny between us!' they cry. Their saddlebags clink.

options.label: 'Then let us pray for some!'
options.log: Robin makes them kneel and pray. Then they all check their bags... and what a miracle! Robin shares out the gold, keeping a little for the poor.

options.label: Throw off the robe
options.log: 'Robin Hood!' The priests swing their purses at him like clubs.

nodes.text: Robin makes the priests swear to be kind to beggars, and sends them on with enough for their supper.

tinker.name: The Tinker's Warrant
tinker.intro: A tinker is going about with a warrant from the Sheriff to arrest Robin Hood. He has no idea what Robin looks like.

nodes.text: Robin finds the tinker at the inn, boasting about his warrant to anyone who'll listen.
'Do you know where Robin Hood is?' asks the tinker.

options.label: Buy him another ale
options.log: Robin buys round after round. The tinker falls asleep, and Robin borrows the warrant and leaves him the bill.

options.label: 'I'm sitting right here!'
options.log: The tinker laughs so hard he falls off his stool. Robin slips the warrant from his bag.

nodes.text: The tinker catches up with Robin in the lane, waving his hammer. 'You owe me a warrant and a bill!'
nodes.win: Robin knocks the tinker's hat over his eyes. The tinker can't stop laughing.
nodes.lose: The tinker bonks Robin on the head with his tool bag. 'Got you!' But he's laughing too hard to hold on.

nodes.text: The tinker tears up the warrant himself. 'A man who pays for my ale is no villain.' He promises to mend the band's pots for life.

pinder.name: The Jolly Pinder of Wakefield
pinder.intro: The Pinder of Wakefield guards the town's fields, and nobody, knight or squire or outlaw, takes a shortcut across them.

nodes.text: Robin and Will take the short way, straight across the corn.
A big man with a big staff blocks the path. 'Back you go, the long way round, the pair of you.'

options.label: 'There are two of us!'
options.log: 'Good,' says the Pinder, 'I was getting bored.'

options.label: Offer to pay for the corn
options.log: 'It's not the corn, it's the rule,' says the Pinder, setting his back to a thorn bush.

nodes.text: The Pinder takes on both of them at once!
nodes.win: Robin and Will finally land him in the hedge. 'Well fought! Come and have bread and ale.'
nodes.lose: The Pinder plants his staff and laughs. 'Had enough? Then come and eat.'

nodes.text: Over bread and ale the Pinder agrees to join the band at Michaelmas, when his year of service ends.

much_miller.name: Much the Miller's Son
much_miller.intro: The miller of Blidworth grinds the poor folk's corn for free. Now the Sheriff has fined him, and his son Much has sent for Robin.

nodes.text: Much, a quick little lad dusted white with flour, leads the outlaws to the mill.
The Sheriff's men are already counting the mill's sacks.

options.label: Hide in the flour sacks
options.log: Robin and Will climb into the flour sacks...

options.label: Stand in the mill door
options.log: 'Put the miller's money back,' says Robin.

nodes.text: The fine is paid back, and the villagers have flour for the winter. Much becomes the band's swiftest messenger.

beggar.name: Robin and the Beggar
beggar.intro: Robin meets a sturdy old beggar at the crossroads with a heavy meal-bag and a heavier staff.

nodes.text: For a joke, Robin asks the beggar to lend him a penny.
'Lend you? I'd sooner lend you a whack!'

options.label: 'Let's see your whack, then'
options.log: The beggar spits on his hands and grips his pikestaff.

options.label: Try to take the bag
options.log: The beggar slaps Robin's hand away. 'Mind your manners!'

nodes.text: The old beggar is quicker than he looks!
nodes.win: Robin tips the beggar onto his own meal-bag, and oatmeal flies everywhere.
nodes.lose: The beggar raps Robin's knuckles until he yelps. 'Respect your elders, lad!'

nodes.text: They make friends, and the beggar teaches Robin how to walk and talk like a beggar, a disguise he will use many times.

shepherd.name: Robin and the Shepherd
shepherd.intro: A shepherd sits by the road with a fine bottle and a fat bag of bread. Robin and Will are very hungry.

nodes.text: 'Share your supper with two hungry travellers?' asks Robin.
The shepherd whistles for his dog. 'Win it off me, if you can.'

options.label: Wager a gold piece
options.log: 'Done!' says the shepherd. 'Loser pays for supper.'

options.label: Wager Robin's horn
options.log: 'Done!' says the shepherd. 'I fancy a horn.'

nodes.text: The shepherd and his dog against Robin and Will!
nodes.win: The dog rolls over for a tummy rub, and the shepherd gives up laughing.
nodes.lose: The dog herds Robin and Will into a pen with the sheep. Baaa!

nodes.text: The shepherd shares his supper anyway, and promises to warn the band whenever the Sheriff's riders cross his meadows.

ranger.name: Robin and the Ranger
ranger.intro: A new ranger guards the King's deer park, and he's sworn to keep Robin Hood out of it.

nodes.text: The ranger finds Robin sitting on the park wall, eating an apple.
'Off that wall, outlaw, or I'll knock you off!'

options.label: Jump down
options.log: Robin jumps down. 'Bows or swords?' 'Swords. Bows are for cowards.' 'We'll see.'

options.label: Throw him the apple core
options.log: It bounces off the ranger's nose. That settles it.

nodes.text: Ranger against outlaw among the deer!
nodes.win: Robin's arrow pins the ranger's cloak to a tree. 'I give up! Well shot!'
nodes.lose: The ranger knocks Robin's bow away. 'Yield?' 'Yield. But you fight like an outlaw.'

nodes.text: The ranger admits the Sheriff pays him badly anyway. He'll look the other way whenever the band passes through.

bold_pedlar.name: The Bold Pedlar
bold_pedlar.intro: A pedlar with a huge pack is walking the road. Will Scarlet wants to know what's in it.

nodes.text: 'What's in the pack, friend?' asks Will. 'Needles, ribbons, buttons... and a stout stick for nosy folk.'
The pedlar sets the pack down and cracks his knuckles.

options.label: Will draws his sword
options.log: 'Swords? I'll use my staff,' grins the pedlar.

options.label: Robin offers to buy a ribbon
options.log: 'No you don't,' says Will. 'I want to fight him!'

nodes.text: Will against the pedlar, with Robin watching and eating an apple.
nodes.win: Will spins the pedlar around until he sits down dizzy.
nodes.lose: The pedlar whacks Will's sword out of his hand. Robin laughs so hard he chokes on the apple.

nodes.text: 'Gamble Gold is my name,' says the pedlar. 'I'm running from the Sheriff myself.' Robin knows the name: he's Robin's own cousin!

poor_knight.name: The Sad Knight
poor_knight.intro: A knight rides by in a shabby cloak, with his hood pulled down and the saddest face in England.

nodes.text: Robin invites the knight to dinner under the greenwood tree. He eats like a man who hasn't had a good meal in weeks.
'I am Sir Richard at the Lee. I owe the Abbot of St Mary's four hundred pounds. If I can't pay by Midsummer, he takes my lands.'

options.label: Lend him the money
options.log: 'Who will stand surety for you?' 'Only Our Lady.' 'Then she is surety enough.' Robin counts out four hundred pounds.

options.label: Lend him the money, and a horse
options.log: Robin lends him the money, a good grey horse and Will as his squire for the road.

nodes.text: Two of the Abbot's spies have been watching from the bushes. They mean to report to the Abbot!
Sir Richard rides away a happier man. 'Within a year I will repay you,' he swears.

robins_larder.name: Robin Hood's Larder
robins_larder.place: The hollow oak called Robin Hood's Larder
robins_larder.intro: Winter is coming. The band fills a great hollow oak with food for the poor families of Sherwood.

nodes.text: Little John hauls sacks of flour, Will rolls cheeses, and Robin counts out the hams.
Snow starts to fall. The band has to drag the last cart through the drifts.
The Sheriff's foresters and hounds have found the larder! 'All this belongs to the Sheriff now!'
The foresters flee through the snow. All winter long, no family in Sherwood goes hungry.

three_keepers.name: Robin Hood's Delight
three_keepers.intro: On a fine May morning, Robin, Little John and Will meet three of the King's keepers, who swear they'll catch an outlaw today.

nodes.text: 'Three of you, three of us,' says Robin. 'Shall we make a morning of it?'
The keepers look at each other, then at Little John's size, and gulp.

options.label: Swords and staves
options.log: 'Agreed!' They pair off across the clearing.

options.label: First to the brook loses
options.log: 'Agreed!' Everyone eyes the muddy brook.

nodes.text: They fight from morning to afternoon, and nobody wants to stop!
nodes.win: The keepers fall over, puffing. 'Enough! We'll buy the drinks!'
nodes.lose: The outlaws flop down, puffing. 'Enough! We'll buy the drinks!'

nodes.text: All six walk to Nottingham arm in arm and spend the evening telling stories at the inn. They call it Robin Hood's Delight.

butcher.name: Robin the Butcher
butcher.intro: Robin buys a butcher's cart, his apron and all his meat, and drives to Nottingham market to sell it.

nodes.text: Robin sells meat at a penny a pound. The other butchers grumble. The townsfolk queue round the square.
The Sheriff thinks this new butcher must be a rich fool. 'Have you any horned beasts to sell, good butcher?'

options.label: 'Hundreds! Come and see.'
options.log: The Sheriff brings three hundred pounds and follows Robin into Sherwood, rubbing his hands.

options.label: Give meat free to widows first
options.log: Every widow in Nottingham goes home with a roast. Then Robin leads the greedy Sheriff into Sherwood.

nodes.text: A herd of deer bounds across the glade. 'There are my horned beasts!' says Robin, and blows his horn.
'It's Robin Hood!' The Sheriff's guards draw their swords.
The Sheriff pays for his dinner with his three hundred pounds and rides home very grumpy.

potter.name: Robin and the Potter
potter.intro: A potter has driven his cart through Sherwood for three years without paying Robin a penny of toll. Little John bets Robin can't make him pay.

nodes.text: Robin steps into the road and grabs the potter's horse. The potter jumps down with a staff.
Robin against the potter, with Little John watching and grinning.
nodes.win: Robin knocks the potter's staff away. They shake hands, laughing.
nodes.lose: The potter knocks Robin flat. Little John wins his bet.

nodes.text: Robin trades clothes with the potter and drives the pots to Nottingham. He sells them so cheap that the Sheriff's wife buys the last five, and asks him to dinner!

options.label: Shoot with the Sheriff's men
options.log: After dinner Robin out-shoots every archer at the Sheriff's butts. 'Who taught you?' 'Robin Hood himself. I could take you to him...'

options.label: Give the lady a gift
options.log: Robin gives the Sheriff's wife a pot of honey. She likes him far better than her husband. 'I could take you to Robin Hood,' he tells the Sheriff.

nodes.text: Deep in Sherwood, the Sheriff and his guards realise who the potter really is!
The Sheriff walks home without his horse. Robin sends the lady a white pony 'from the potter', and pays the real potter ten pounds for his pots.

reynold_greenleaf.name: Little John in the Sheriff's House
reynold_greenleaf.intro: Little John shoots in the Sheriff's contest under the name Reynold Greenleaf. He shoots so well that the Sheriff hires him as a servant!

nodes.text: One morning the Sheriff goes hunting. Little John wakes up late and very hungry, and the steward won't give him breakfast.
The kitchen door is locked.

options.label: Knock it down
options.log: CRASH! John eats a whole pie, a loaf and a ham.

options.label: Climb through the window
options.log: John squeezes through the window, gets stuck, gets unstuck, and eats a whole pie.

nodes.text: The Sheriff's cook comes at John with a ladle and a sword!
nodes.win: John sits the cook in his own flour bin. 'You're the best fighter in this house!' gasps the cook.
nodes.lose: The cook bops John on the head with the ladle. 'You're the best fighter I've met!' gasps John.

nodes.text: The cook wants to join the outlaws. Together they pack up the Sheriff's silver plates and four hundred pounds.
A guard spots them carrying sacks of silver out of the back door!

sheriff_dinner.name: The Sheriff Dines in Sherwood
sheriff_dinner.intro: Little John goes looking for the Sheriff, who is still out hunting and has no idea his silver has gone.

nodes.text: 'Master!' cries John. 'I've seen a green hart with seven score deer behind him! Come and see!'
The Sheriff follows John deep into the forest, straight to Robin's camp.

options.label: Serve dinner on his own silver
options.log: The Sheriff stares at his own silver plates, holding his own roast. He loses his appetite.

options.label: Let him sleep under the stars
options.log: The Sheriff spends a cold night on the ground in his shirt. 'I'd give anything for my own feather bed!'

nodes.text: The Sheriff's escort finally catches up and charges into the camp!
The Sheriff swears an oath never to harm the band again. Nobody believes him, but he goes home very quietly.

four_beggars.name: Little John and the Four Beggars
four_beggars.intro: Little John borrows a palmer's robe and goes begging along the road, to see what he can learn.

nodes.text: He meets four beggars: one blind, one deaf, one dumb and one lame.
'Give us something, brother!' says the dumb one. The blind one is counting coins.

options.label: 'Let's share what we have'
options.log: John opens his empty purse. The beggars scowl. 'You're no use. Clear off!'

options.label: 'I thought you were blind?'
options.log: The blind beggar blushes. The lame one jumps up. The dumb one shouts 'Get him!'

nodes.text: The sham beggars attack Little John!
Their ragged cloaks are sewn full of gold! The blind run, the lame leap a hedge, and John shares the gold out among the real poor of Blidworth.

scotsman.name: Robin and the Scotsman
scotsman.intro: A huge Scotsman has come south to join Robin Hood's band. He says he can beat anyone in it.

nodes.text: 'Anyone?' says Little John, rolling up his sleeves.
A crowd gathers on the bridge to watch.

options.label: Staves
options.log: 'Staves it is!' The Scotsman twirls a staff as long as a boat.

options.label: Fists
options.log: 'Fists, then!' Robin says they'd better use staves, so nobody loses a tooth.

nodes.text: Little John against the Scotsman, in the middle of the bridge!
nodes.win: SPLASH! The Scotsman goes into the river. He comes up laughing.
nodes.lose: SPLASH! Little John goes into the river, just like the old days.

nodes.text: The Scotsman joins the band, and the crowd go home talking about the best fight they've ever seen.

three_pedlars.name: Robin and the Three Pedlars
three_pedlars.place: The road by the toll bridge
three_pedlars.intro: Three pedlars walk the road with heavy packs. 'They must be carrying something good,' says Will.

nodes.text: Robin calls to them to stop. They walk faster.
Robin shoots an arrow into the leading pedlar's pack. Out pours a cloud of sweet-smelling herbs.

options.label: Apologise
options.log: 'Sorry about your pack,' says Robin. 'Sorry about your head,' say the pedlars, raising their staves.

options.label: Call them to fight
options.log: The pedlars drop their packs and raise their staves.

nodes.text: Three pedlars against three outlaws!
nodes.win: The pedlars sit down in the road. 'You win! Have some of our healing balm.'
nodes.lose: The outlaws are black and blue. The pedlars rub their healing balm on every bruise.

nodes.text: The pedlars sell healing herbs, and now they'll sell them to the band at half price.

noble_fisherman.name: The Noble Fisherman
noble_fisherman.intro: Robin wonders if a fisherman's life is easier than an outlaw's. He rides to Scarborough and hires on a fishing boat as 'Simon'.

nodes.text: Simon is the worst fisherman the boat has ever seen. He tangles every line.
A French pirate ship comes alongside! The fishermen shake with fear.

options.label: 'Tie me to the mast!'
options.log: 'So the waves don't throw off my aim,' says Simon, stringing his bow.

options.label: Climb into the rigging
options.log: Simon climbs the mast like a squirrel and strings his bow.

nodes.text: The pirates swing aboard with cutlasses!
The pirates jump back to their ship and sail away, leaving a chest of gold behind. Robin gives half to the fishermen, and half to the poor of Scarborough.

knight_pays_abbot.name: The Knight and the Abbot
knight_pays_abbot.intro: It's Midsummer. Sir Richard rides to St Mary's Abbey to pay his debt, and the band comes along in disguise.

nodes.text: Sir Richard comes before the Abbot in his old, shabby cloak. The Abbot rubs his hands.
'Have you brought my money, knight? No? Then your lands are mine!'

options.label: Pour out the gold
options.log: Sir Richard pours four hundred pounds onto the table. 'Not one penny more.' The Abbot turns purple.

options.label: Make him beg first
options.log: Sir Richard pleads for more time, and the Abbot laughs. Then the knight pours the gold onto the table. The Abbot turns purple.

nodes.text: 'Guards! Throw them out and keep the gold!'
Sir Richard rides home free and clear. 'Now I must save up to repay Robin,' he says.

cellarer.name: Our Lady Repays
cellarer.intro: The High Cellarer of St Mary's Abbey rides through Sherwood with a great train of packhorses.

nodes.text: Little John bows deeply and invites the monks to dinner with Robin Hood.
'Our Lady stood surety for a loan to a knight,' says Robin. 'Perhaps she's sent the money with you. How much do you carry?' 'Only twenty marks,' says the cellarer.

options.label: Search the saddlebags
options.log: Little John counts eight hundred pounds! 'Our Lady has paid us twice over,' says Robin.

options.label: Take him at his word
options.log: Robin trusts him, but a bag splits open, and gold coins roll everywhere.

nodes.text: The cellarer's guards draw their swords!
The monks ride on, lighter by a fortune. The band shares it among every poor village in Sherwood.

knight_returns.name: Sir Richard Keeps His Word
knight_returns.intro: A year has passed. Sir Richard rides to Sherwood to repay Robin, bringing a hundred fine bows as a gift. On the way, he passes a wrestling match.

nodes.text: A poor yeoman has won the wrestling, but the bad losers are trying to cheat him out of his prize.
Sir Richard stops his horse. Little John is with him as an escort.

options.label: Stand by the yeoman
options.log: Sir Richard stands beside the yeoman. 'The prize is his. Who says otherwise?'

options.label: Wrestle the champion
options.log: Little John offers to wrestle the champion of the bad losers.

nodes.text: Little John wrestles the champion!
nodes.win: Little John flips the champion head over heels. The crowd roars.
nodes.lose: The champion pins Little John, but shakes his hand. 'The yeoman won fair.'

nodes.text: The bad losers set their hired men on Sir Richard!
Sir Richard arrives in Sherwood late, with four hundred pounds and a hundred bows. Robin won't take the money: Our Lady already paid it!

widows_sons.name: The Widow's Three Sons
widows_sons.intro: A widow weeps on the road. Her three sons were caught taking the King's deer to feed their family, and the Sheriff means to make an example of them.

nodes.text: Robin swaps clothes with an old pilgrim and hobbles to the crossroads.
The Sheriff is there with his guards and the three frightened brothers.

options.label: Offer to be the Sheriff's helper
options.log: 'I'll do the job for a shilling,' says the 'old pilgrim'. The Sheriff agrees, and Robin steps up beside the brothers.

options.label: Blow the horn at once
options.log: Robin blows three blasts. A hundred outlaws come running over the hill!

nodes.text: 'It's Robin Hood! Seize him!'
Robin cuts the brothers free, and they run home to their mother. All three join the band.
The band melts into the trees before more soldiers arrive.

will_stutly.name: The Rescue of Will Stutly
will_stutly.intro: Will Stutly, one of the band, was spying in Nottingham in a friar's robe. The Sheriff caught him, and means to lock him away forever.

nodes.text: The band comes to Nottingham disguised as pilgrims and beggars, and waits by the gate.
The Sheriff's men march Will Stutly out of the gate in chains.

options.label: Little John grabs Stutly
options.log: Little John strolls up, cuts Stutly's ropes, and hands him a sword. 'You didn't think we'd leave you, did you?'

options.label: Robin shouts a challenge
options.log: Robin throws back his pilgrim's hood. The guards gasp.

nodes.text: The guards fight to keep their prisoner!
More soldiers pour out of the gate as the band runs for the trees!

bishop_old_woman.name: The Bishop and the Old Woman
bishop_old_woman.place: An old woman's cottage near Blidworth
bishop_old_woman.intro: The Bishop of Hereford is hunting Robin through the woods. Robin runs into the cottage of an old woman he once helped.

nodes.text: 'Quick!' says the old woman. 'Give me your green clothes and put on my grey dress!'
Robin walks right past the Bishop's men in a grey dress and bonnet.

options.label: Curtsey to the Bishop
options.log: Robin curtseys. 'Good day, your Grace.' The Bishop doesn't even look.

options.label: Ask the Bishop for a penny
options.log: 'Away, old hag!' snaps the Bishop. Robin hides his giggles.

nodes.text: The Bishop's men drag the 'outlaw' out of the cottage: the old woman, in Robin's green, laughing her head off.
Robin's horn sounds from the hill, and the band charges down!
The Bishop pays for the old woman's new roof, and Friar Tuck makes him say sorry to her, twice.

bishop_dinner.name: The Bishop's Supper
bishop_dinner.intro: The Bishop of Hereford is riding through Sherwood again. Robin and his men dress as shepherds and roast a fine supper beside the road.

nodes.text: The Bishop smells the roast. 'Shepherds, roasting the King's deer? I'll have you all arrested!'
'Mercy, my lord!' says Robin, and blows his horn.

options.label: Invite him to supper
options.log: The Bishop eats three helpings. Then Robin hands him the bill.

options.label: Ask Alan for a song first
options.log: Alan plays a jig so lively that the Bishop's feet start tapping all by themselves.

nodes.text: The Bishop's knight and guards won't let him pay!
The Bishop pays the bill (the whole contents of his saddlebags) and then, for good measure, dances a jig around the oak while Alan plays.

monk_of_nottingham.name: Robin Hood and the Monk
monk_of_nottingham.intro: Robin wants to hear Mass in St Mary's church in Nottingham. Little John warns him not to go alone, but Robin goes anyway.

nodes.text: Robin kneels at the back of the church. A monk he once robbed on the road looks round, and his eyes go wide.
The monk slips out of the side door, running for the Sheriff.

options.label: Finish his prayers
options.log: Robin finishes his prayers. By then, the church doors are full of soldiers.

options.label: Run after the monk
options.log: Robin runs for the door, but it slams shut in his face.

nodes.text: Robin fights alone in the churchyard!
Over the churchyard wall and through the streets! Little John and the band are waiting at the gate.
'I told you so,' says Little John. Robin admits he was right, and buys him supper for a week.

guy_horsehide.name: Guy of Gisborne
guy_horsehide.intro: Robin dreams of two strong yeomen who beat him and bind him. When he wakes, he goes to find them. Instead he finds a man dressed in a horse's hide.

nodes.text: The stranger has a horse's hide over his armour, tail and mane and all. He's looking for someone.
'I'm hunting Robin Hood,' he says. 'Shall we shoot a match while I wait for him?'

options.label: Shoot at the garland
options.log: They set up a rose garland at sixty paces. Robin's arrow splits the wand down the middle.

options.label: Tell him who you are
options.log: 'I am Robin Hood.' The stranger throws back the hide. 'And I am Guy of Gisborne!'

nodes.text: Sir Guy blows a whistle, and his trackers leap out of the bracken!
Sir Guy lands in the bracken, out cold. Robin borrows his horse-hide cloak and his silver horn. He has an idea.

john_rescued.name: Robin in Guy's Cloak
john_rescued.intro: While Robin met Sir Guy, the Sheriff caught Little John. He's tied to a tree at the crossroads.

nodes.text: Robin, wrapped in Guy's horse hide, blows Guy's silver horn.
'That's Sir Guy's horn!' cries the Sheriff. 'He's caught Robin Hood! Ask any reward, Sir Guy!'

options.label: 'Let me deal with the prisoner'
options.log: Robin strides to Little John, cuts his ropes and hands him Guy's bow.

options.label: 'Just the outlaw on the tree'
options.log: The Sheriff waves him over. Robin slices John free. 'Took your time,' says John.

nodes.text: The Sheriff sees the face under the hood. 'It's Robin Hood!' The rest of the band bursts out of the trees.
The Sheriff gallops all the way back to Nottingham without stopping, and Sir Guy has to walk home without his cloak.

queens_match.name: Queen Katherine's Archers
queens_match.intro: The Queen has made a wager with the King: her archers will beat his. She secretly sends for Robin Hood to shoot on her side.

nodes.text: Robin, Little John and Will ride to London dressed in scarlet, and the Queen hides them among her men.
The King's champions shoot first, and every arrow hits the gold.

options.label: Ask the King for safety first
options.log: 'Whoever shoots on my side,' says the Queen, 'may go home safe.' The King agrees, chuckling.

options.label: Just shoot
options.log: Robin steps up to the mark without a word.

nodes.text: The Queen's archers against the King's!
nodes.win: Robin's last arrow splits the King's champion's arrow. The Queen claps with delight.
nodes.lose: The King's champions edge it by a whisker, but the Queen says she's never seen finer shooting.

nodes.text: Robin kneels and gives his name. The King frowns, but a promise is a promise: forty days to go home safe.

robins_chase.name: Robin Hood's Chase
robins_chase.intro: The forty days are over, and the King himself rides north to catch Robin Hood.

nodes.text: The King reaches Sherwood. Robin has gone to Yorkshire.
The King follows to Yorkshire. Robin has gone to Lancashire. The King's horse is very tired.
The King's knights finally catch up on the Great North Road!
Robin doubles back to London to ask the Queen for help. The King, footsore and laughing, gives up the chase. 'That fellow leads me a merry dance!'

prince_of_aragon.name: The Prince of Aragon
prince_of_aragon.intro: A proud prince from Aragon has come to London with two giant champions. Unless three men can beat them, he will carry off the King's young cousin to be his bride.

nodes.text: Nobody in London dares to fight. Then three pilgrims step out of the crowd.
The princess looks hopefully at the three pilgrims. The giants laugh.

options.label: Throw off the pilgrim robes
options.log: Robin, Little John and Will throw off their robes. The crowd roars.

options.label: Fight in disguise
options.log: The pilgrims pick up their staves. The giants stop laughing.

nodes.text: Three outlaws against the prince's champions!
The giants flee back to Aragon with their proud prince. The princess is free, and the King of England thanks three 'pilgrims' with a bag of gold.

castle_siege.name: The Siege of Castle Lee
castle_siege.place: Sir Richard's castle at the Lee
castle_siege.intro: After the silver arrow, Sir Richard shelters the whole band in his castle. The Sheriff's army surrounds it.

nodes.text: Sir Richard pulls up the drawbridge. 'You saved my lands. Now my walls will save you.'
The Sheriff calls up at the walls: 'Hand over the outlaws!'

options.label: 'Only the King may ask that'
options.log: 'Only the King may tell me who to shelter!' calls Sir Richard. The Sheriff stamps his foot.

options.label: Pelt them with apples
options.log: Alan sings a rude song about the Sheriff, while Tuck pelts the soldiers with apples.

nodes.text: The Sheriff's men storm the gate!
The Sheriff's army gives up and marches home to ask the King for help. The band slips back to Sherwood.

sir_richard_rescue.name: The Rescue of Sir Richard
sir_richard_rescue.intro: The Sheriff has caught Sir Richard out hawking and is taking him to Nottingham in chains. His lady rides to Sherwood to beg Robin's help.

nodes.text: 'Our Lady is your friend, Robin,' says the Lady of the Lee. 'Help my husband for her sake.'
Robin calls every man in the band. The Sheriff's party is on the road below.

options.label: Charge down the hill
options.log: A hundred and forty outlaws charge down the hill in Lincoln green!

options.label: Block the road with a tree
options.log: Little John drops an oak across the road. The Sheriff's horses skid to a halt.

nodes.text: The Sheriff will not give up his prisoner!
Sir Richard is free! The Sheriff flees so fast that he leaves his hat in the road, and he isn't seen in Sherwood for a long time.

kings_ransom.name: The King's Ransom
kings_ransom.intro: King Richard is held captive across the sea. Everyone has paid a ransom tax to free him, but Prince John's men are keeping the silver for themselves.

nodes.text: Carts loaded with the ransom silver roll into Nottingham Castle, never to leave.
'That silver is meant to bring the King home,' says Robin.

options.label: Ambush the carts at the gate
options.log: The band hides in the hay carts going into the castle.

options.label: Sneak in at night
options.log: The band climbs the castle rock in the dark...

nodes.text: Prince John's tax men and their guards!
The silver goes to Queen Eleanor, who sends it straight on to bring her son home.
The band rides out of Nottingham with the carts empty and their hearts full.

king_in_sherwood.name: The King Comes to Sherwood
king_in_sherwood.intro: King Richard is home. He hears that Robin Hood rules Sherwood, and decides to see for himself, disguised as a tall abbot.

nodes.text: Robin stops a tall abbot on the road and invites him to dinner, as the band always does.
After a feast of venison, the band shoots at a rose garland. Whoever misses gets a buffet from the abbot.

options.label: Robin shoots last
options.log: Robin's arrow misses the garland by three fingers. 'Abbot, I'll take my buffet.'

options.label: Robin shoots first
options.log: Robin misses the garland for the first time in his life. 'Abbot, I'll take my buffet.'

nodes.text: The tall abbot rolls up his sleeves. His arms are like oak trees.
nodes.win: Robin ducks the buffet, and the abbot spins round and falls on his bottom. He laughs louder than anyone.
nodes.lose: The abbot's buffet knocks Robin flat on the grass! 'Who hits that hard?' says Robin, and looks up into the face of the King.

nodes.text: The abbot throws off his hood: it is King Richard! The whole band kneels. The King pardons every one of them, and there is a feast in Sherwood that lasts all night.
